question: The likelihood of a neutral atom gaining an electron is known as:
solution:
The likelihood of a neutral atom gaining an electron is known as __**electron affinity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electron affinity** is defined as the amount of energy released when a neutral atom in the gaseous phase gains an electron to form a negative ion.
 
• This property is an indication of the** ability of an atom to accept an electron**.
 
• Higher electron affinity values indicate a greater tendency to gain an electron.
 
• Electron affinity generally increases across a period and decreases down a group in the periodic table.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electronegativity** is a measure of the tendency of an atom to attract a bonding pair of electrons.
 
• **Electro positivity** is the ability of an element to donate electrons and form positive ions.
 
• Electron affinity is different from electronegativity, which is a measure of the ability of an atom to attract electrons in a chemical bond.
 
• Elements with high electron affinities tend to be non-metals, as they are more likely to gain electrons.
